run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The failing path is the frontend's recommendations endpoint. Between about 14:10:16Z and 14:11:31Z, frontend spans 'GET /api/recommendations' ran to a 15 s cutoff (HTTP 200 returned to the proxy) while frontend-proxy and load-generator spans on the same requests ended as 504 errors; the frontend's own 'oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' client spans for those requests stayed open for 62-129 s and finally failed with rpc status 14 'UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ETIMEDOUT 10.96.23.220:8080', and the enclosing frontend spans recorded HTTP 500. 10.96.23.220 is the ClusterIP of Service 'recommendation' (port 8080), whose only endpoint is Pod recommendation-5cdbdff544-mjdws (10.244.234.186, node sregym-worker). That pod reported Running/Ready with 0 restarts and its completed server spans were fast (p95 12.3 ms for RecommendationService/ListRecommendations), so the failure is TCP reachability to the recommendation pod (connect timed out, not refused), not slow request handling in recommendation. Other frontend routes and other services on the same node (cart p95 4.75 ms, product-catalog p95 18.9 ms for GetProduct) were fast, and all flagd demo flags are set to 'off', so neither a node-wide fault nor a flag-injected failure explains it. The mechanism behind the dropped SYNs (network policy/blackhole versus the recommendation app no longer accepting connections) and the object that injected it could not be determined: the recommendation container defines no probes, no chaos/experiment CRD is installed and Calico/AdminNetworkPolicy objects are not readable with the permitted kinds.

claims.text: Frontend spans 'GET /api/recommendations' started between 14:10:16Z and 14:11:23Z ran ~15.0 s and were recorded error=true with http.status_code=500, while frontend-proxy 'GET' spans (http.status_code="504", otel.status_code=ERROR) and load-generator 'GET' spans (504) on the same traces lasted ~15.0 s; the frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' spans record error="true", http.status_code="0".

For those requests the frontend's own client spans 'oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' remained open for 62,407,752-128,973,997 us and ended with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ETIMEDOUT 10.96.23.220:8080 (2026-11-21T14:12:25.398Z)'; the parent 'executing api route (pages) /api/recommendations' and 'GET /api/recommendations' spans carry http.status_code 500 / otel.status_code ERROR.

Over the 5 minutes ending 14:11:31Z the mean span duration of frontend 'GET /api/recommendations' was 5,239.65 ms and of load-generator 'user_get_recommendations' 7,591.87 ms, while all other frontend/load-generator operations stayed in the tens of milliseconds.
ClusterIP 10.96.23.220 is Service 'recommendation' (type ClusterIP, port 8080 named tcp-service, targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=recommendation).

The 'recommendation' Service has exactly one ready endpoint, Pod recommendation-5cdbdff544-mjdws at 10.244.234.186 on node sregym-worker; the pod was Running with ready=true and restartCount 0 at 14:11:34Z.

The recommendation container in Deployment 'recommendation' defines no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe (only a 500Mi memory limit), so its Ready condition and Service endpoint membership do not by themselves confirm that the server accepted connections.

The recommendation pod template was changed during the window: Deployment 'recommendation' now has nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=sregym-worker and template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-21T14:09:40Z; ReplicaSets recommendation-5bb649dccb (created 14:08:04Z), recommendation-6b9dd6f6fc (created 14:09:01Z, nodeSelector sregym-worker) and recommendation-5cdbdff544 (created 14:09:40Z) all use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-recommendation and identical env.
The current recommendation pod logged 'Recommendation service started, listening on port 8080' at 14:09:43Z and wrote no further lines up to 14:11:31Z (2 log lines read in total).

Recommendation's own completed spans were fast over the 5 minutes to 14:11:31Z: p95 12.32 ms for 'oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' and 'get_product_list', 5.77 ms for 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts', and no ERROR-status spans were returned for service recommendation.

Frontend calls on other routes were fast in the same 5-minute window (p95 9.85 ms 'GET /api/products/{productId}', 4.75 ms 'oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 21.0 ms 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct', 71.3 ms 'GET /'), and product-catalog GetProduct p95 was 18.9 ms, so only the recommendations route exceeded 1 s.

In ConfigMap 'flagd-config' (key demo.flagd.json) every demo flag - including recommendationCacheFailure, productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, adFailure, paymentFailure, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak and kafkaQueueProblems - has defaultVariant 'off'; no fault variant is in effect.

Nodes sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2 and sregym-worker3 were all Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable = False, and sregym-worker (hosting the recommendation pod) carries no taints and is not unschedulable.

No Unhealthy or Killing event names the recommendation pods; the only Unhealthy pod events in the window are grafana (readiness probe, 14:08:11Z), opensearch-0 (startup probe, 14:08:33Z) and otel-collector-agent (readiness probe, 14:08:06Z), plus loki-0 in namespace observe.
The recommendation pod's memory working set stayed flat at about 79 MB (limit 500Mi) from 14:09:00Z to 14:11:30Z, showing no growth toward an OOM.

Earlier frontend errors in the window (14:08:10Z-14:08:25Z) were startup-time 'ECONNREFUSED' failures to other ClusterIPs (10.96.156.96, 10.96.210.13, 10.96.202.11, 10.96.233.63, 10.96.121.81:3551) from the previous frontend pod frontend-6859c775df-6bk5v, a different failure mode from the later ETIMEDOUT to the recommendation ClusterIP.

TCP connections from the frontend to the recommendation pod were blackholed from about 14:10:16Z: the dial to Service ClusterIP 10.96.23.220:8080 (single endpoint Pod recommendation-5cdbdff544-mjdws, 10.244.234.186) timed out instead of being refused, so SYNs to that pod went unanswered while the pod stayed Running/Ready and its other traffic (calls to product-catalog) kept working. The candidate mechanisms are a policy/route drop targeting that pod's port 8080 or the pod's listen/accept queue no longer being served; the evidence does not separate them.

The recommendation pod re-placement at 14:09:01Z/14:09:40Z (nodeSelector sregym-worker plus restartedAt, new ReplicaSet recommendation-5cdbdff544) is the change that immediately precedes the connectivity failure, but on the evidence it is only a preceding change: the pod's replacement completed and the fault (unanswered SYNs to the pod IP) is not explained by the rollout itself.

The recommendation pod itself shows no failure evidence: it was Running/ready with 0 restarts, had no Unhealthy/Killing events, its memory was flat near 79 MB, and its completed server spans were fast with no ERROR status, so recommendation's request handling was not slow or erroring.
Flag-injected failure (for example recommendationCacheFailure, productCatalogFailure or failedReadinessProbe) is rejected: every flag in flagd-config demo.flagd.json has defaultVariant 'off'.

A node-level or cluster-network-wide fault on sregym-worker is rejected: the node is Ready with no pressure or taints, and other frontend calls to pods on the same node were fast (cart p95 4.75 ms, ProductCatalog GetProduct p95 21 ms from frontend, product-reviews serving requests).

Advisory: verify from a host or debug pod whether SYNs to 10.244.234.186:8080 (and to ClusterIP 10.96.23.220:8080) are dropped or answered, and inspect Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy/AdminNetworkPolicy and any network-emulation applied to the recommendation pod, since that is what separates a policy blackhole from an exhausted accept queue.
Advisory: add a readinessProbe to the recommendation Deployment so that a pod that stops accepting connections is removed from the Service endpoints instead of silently blackholing frontend traffic.

gaps: No NetworkPolicy objects exist in the cluster (a cluster-wide query for kind networkpolicies returned no items), and the Calico/AdminNetworkPolicy CRDs (globalnetworkpolicies, networkpolicies.crd.projectcalico.org, adminnetworkpolicies) cannot be read with the permitted resource kinds, so whether a policy blocks traffic to recommendation-5cdbdff544-mjdws could not be verified.

No chaos/experiment CRD is installed (the CRD list contains only Calico and OpenEBS kinds), and the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so the object that caused the connectivity fault could not be identified.

Because the recommendation container has no probes and pod exec is unavailable, it could not be verified whether its gRPC server was still accepting on port 8080 at 14:10-14:12; the 'listening on port 8080' log line is from 14:09:43Z.

The failing client spans only completed at 14:12:25Z, after the authorized window end (14:11:31Z), so error-rate metrics after the window could not be evaluated; at 14:11:31Z the span metrics still showed STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate 0 for every service (except two zero-valued load-generator/frontend-proxy series).

Frontend application logs inside the window contain only startup lines (168 further lines fall after 14:11:31Z and were not read), and the recommendation container produced no per-request log lines, so no application-level error text from the recommendation side is available.

Whether the fault also affected the recommendation pod's own outbound calls could not be settled: the 1-minute increase series for recommendation spans show aliased values (16, 16, 0, 5.33, 5.33), so exact onset and continuation of recommendation traffic around 14:10-14:11Z remain uncertain.
next_steps: Have a human check Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy/AdminNetworkPolicy/Felix configuration and any host-level iptables/tc rules applied to pod recommendation-5cdbdff544-mjdws (10.244.234.186) during 14:09-14:12Z.
Reproduce with a pod on node sregym-worker2 dialling 10.96.23.220:8080 and 10.244.234.186:8080 while the fault is active to confirm one-way versus two-way packet loss.
Confirm whether the recommendation process was accepting connections at the time (e.g. ss -ltn / netstat Recv-Q on the pod) once exec access is available.

view.cannot_prove: A line that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only limit lines are shown (the newest), and retention, ingest delay, the label selector and line filters can leave gaps. The timestamp is when the line was ingested or parsed, not necessarily when the event happened. A metric query counts only lines inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
